newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Canada's Chretien ends three-day Philippine visit.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Chretien ends three-day Philippine visit.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien left the Philippines on Thursday after a three-day state visit during which he took over chairmanship of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.
Canadian Embassy officials said Chretien had left for Bangkok, the third and final stop on his three-nation Asian tour that earlier took him to Seoul.

He was accompanied by 350 business leaders from engineering construction firms, wheat traders, aircraft manufacturers, telecommunications equipment makers and education companies. They inked deals worth $36 million while in the Philippines and reached agreements in principle worth another $469 million.
Both Canadian and Filipino government officials called the Manila visit a success that had paved the way for increased economic relations between the two countries.
But a Filipino leftist group, Bagong Alyansang Makabayan, or New Nationalist Alliance, charged that Chretien's visit spelled disaster for the Philippines.

"His trade mission is nothing but an all-out effort by a junior imperialist partner to grab a share of the (Philippine) economic pie...," the group said in a statement issued as it picketed the hotel where Chretien was staying.

On Tuesday, Chretien formally took over the role of APEC chairman at a handover ceremony at the Malacanang presidential palace, where Philippine President Fidel Ramos handed him the 18-nation forum's flag and gavel.
Canada is to host the next APEC summit in Vancouver in November. The trade grouping held its previous summit in the Philippines in November last year.

APEC groups Australia, the United States, Canada, Mexico, Chile, Japan, China, Hong Kong, Taiwan, South Korea, Indonesia, Brunei, the Philippines, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Papua New Guinea and New Zealand.
